target.title: fix(file-transfer): don't inline zero-byte files as image content blocks
target.body:
Related: #98673

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where fetching a zero-byte file with an image extension (`.png`/`.jpg`/`.webp`/`.gif`) through the `file_fetch` tool produced a tool-result image content block with no actual image data, which providers cannot render and which some replay paths (before other guards) drop silently — the model just sees nothing useful for that fetch.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is one traced root cause of #98673 ("tool results become invisible to the model"). `file_fetch`'s remote MIME detection (`detectMimeImpl` in `packages/media-core`) falls back to the extension-derived MIME type when content-sniffing an empty buffer finds nothing to sniff — there are no magic bytes in a zero-byte file. So fetching an empty `.png` yields `{ mimeType: "image/png", base64: "" }` from the remote node, and `file-fetch-tool.ts` inlined that directly as `{ type: "image", data: "", mimeType: "image/png" }` in the tool result with no guard. That block is then handed straight to the provider within the same tool-call turn — OpenClaw's replay-time image sanitizer only runs once per attempt on prior persisted history, not on tool results produced mid-turn, so an unguarded construction site like this is the only line of defense.

The fix requires a non-empty payload before treating a fetch as an inline image; a zero-byte (or otherwise payload-less) image-mime fetch now falls through to the same "saved at `<path>`" text notice already used for every other non-inlined file — the file is still saved and still reachable via its returned path, only the model-facing content block shape changes.

I checked the sibling `dir-fetch-tool.ts` surface, which also imports `IMAGE_MIME_INLINE_SET`: it only uses that set to order `mediaUrls` metadata for channel delivery and never constructs a `{type:"image", data}` block in its model-visible `content`, so it does not share this defect.

## User Impact

Fetching an empty or unreadable image-named file via `file_fetch` no longer produces an invisible/unusable image block in the model's context — the model instead sees a normal text confirmation that the (empty) file was fetched and saved.

## Evidence

- New regression tests in `extensions/file-transfer/src/tools/file-fetch-tool.test.ts`:
  - `falls back to text for a zero-byte file with an image-extension mimeType`
  - `still inlines a non-empty image payload` (confirms real images are unaffected)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/file-transfer/src/tools/file-fetch-tool.test.ts` — 3/3 passed.
